slides.highlight: Faraday Future is implementing immersive summer camps for students in Los Angeles to advance embodied AI robotics education, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied learning.

slides.title: China unveils humanoid AI 'companion robots' to ease loneliness
slides.highlight: The development of humanoid AI companion robots to address loneliness is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: On the Structure of Address in Multi-Party Dialogue: From Discrete Labels to Continuous Levels
slides.tldr: CONTINUOUS ADDRESSEE DETECTION IN MULTI-PARTY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This research explores addressee detection as a continuous phenomenon rather than discrete labels, analyzing its relationship with listener behaviors like gaze and backchannels. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: Addressee detection is better modeled as a continuous level than as discrete labels in multi-party dialogue.
card.key_idea: A latent-variable model transforms categorical annotator labels into continuous address levels, representing addressivity as a graded property rather than a multi-class classification task.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Japanese triadic dialogue corpus using GLMMs; continuous levels showed better predictive fit (ELPD) for turn-taking, gaze, and backchannels.
card.limitation: Data is limited to Japanese triadic discussions; address levels were inferred from only three categorical annotations per turn.

slides.title: PACE: Persona Adaptation through Conversational Elicitation in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC PERSONA ADAPTATION FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework for humanoid robots to dynamically synthesize tailored, psychologically grounded personas through user interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: PACE enables humanoid robots to dynamically generate tailored personas through interactive Q&A with users.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using adaptive Q&A to extract psychological dimensions (traits, values, motivations), compiling them into a structured PersonaSpec that governs both LLM dialogue and Ameca robot's facial expressions.
card.evaluation: Tested with 25 participants against a static baseline using BFI-44, economic games, and Likert scales. Results showed significant improvements in persona fidelity and interaction quality.
card.limitation: Relies on cloud-based inference and ASR, potentially introducing latency and transcription errors in noisy environments.

slides.title: Analysis of Mutual and Referential Human and Robot Gazes in a Collaborative Word Association Game
slides.highlight: This study examines how mutual and referential robot gaze affects human visual attention and confirmation-seeking behavior during a collaborative game, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Robot gaze orientation does not significantly affect human visual attention during a cognitively demanding collaborative game.
card.key_idea: A NAO robot used LLM-driven dialogue to play a word association game, manipulating mutual and referential gaze to observe effects on human fixation times and confirmation-seeking behavior.
card.evaluation: 10 non-native English speakers were tested using Tobii Glasses 3; results showed no significant effect of robot gaze on first fixation time.
card.limitation: Small sample size (N=10) and high cognitive load from non-native language use may have skewed results.

slides.title: Knowing You at First Glance: Inferring Apparent Personality from Faces
slides.tldr: FACIAL PERSONALITY INFERENCE FOR EMBODIED AGENTS
slides.highlight: The GlanceFace framework infers apparent personality from facial images to support adaptive initial interaction strategies for embodied agents, aligning with RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: GlanceFace infers perceived MBTI personality types from facial images using VLM-derived semantic priors.
card.key_idea: Combines a Semantic-Enhanced Facial Representation module for capturing subtle cues via VLM embeddings with an uncertainty-aware learning strategy to handle subjective, noisy personality annotations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MBTI benchmarks using person- and image-level protocols. Outperformed baselines (e.g., ArcFace, AdaFace) in Top-K accuracy, F1-score, and AUC.
card.limitation: Predicts perceived impressions rather than intrinsic personality; risks include demographic bias, privacy concerns, and potential misuse in profiling.

slides.title: CF-Net: Conflict Fusion with Speaker Normalisation and Certainty Weighting for Ambivalence/Hesitancy Recognition
slides.highlight: CF-Net utilizes cross-modal incongruence and speaker normalization to detect ambivalence and hesitancy, contributing to HyECHO's goals of multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: CF-Net recognizes ambivalence and hesitancy by explicitly modeling cross-modal incongruence using frozen multimodal backbones.
card.key_idea: Uses ConflictFusion (pairwise absolute-difference features), per-speaker normalization to remove identity offsets, and certainty-weighted focal loss with an auxiliary regression head to handle annotation ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BAH dataset; achieved 0.7155 validation Macro F1 and 0.7364 private test Macro F1, outperforming several 10th ABAW challenge methods.
card.limitation: Relies on frozen backbones and a fixed concatenation fusion strategy rather than learned cross-modal attention.

slides.title: Real-time Generation of Listener Nodding via Prediction of Kinematic Parameters for Avatar Dialogue Systems
slides.highlight: This research proposes a model for predicting the timing and kinematic parameters of listener nodding in real time, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A real-time model for conversational avatars that predicts both the timing and kinematic parameters of nodding.
card.key_idea: A dyadic attention network using Continuous Mimi Encoders and multi-task learning to predict nodding onset, range, speed, repetitions, and swing-up based on speaker-listener speech signals.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via five-fold cross-validation and subjective user studies (n=60); outperformed stochastic and fixed-motion baselines in human-likeness, attentiveness, and naturalness.
card.limitation: Subjective evaluations were conducted via pre-recorded videos as third-party observers rather than through direct face-to-face interactions.

slides.title: CausalGraphX: A Counterfactual Graph Neural Network Framework for Explainable Systemic Risk Assessment
slides.tldr: EXPLAINABLE SYSTEMIC RISK ASSESSMENT VIA COUNTERFACTUAL GNNs
slides.highlight: CausalGraphX uses counterfactual reasoning and Graph Neural Networks to model cascading defaults in financial networks, supporting the MIMIC goal of societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: CausalGraphX uses GNNs and counterfactual reasoning to predict and explain systemic risk in financial networks.
card.key_idea: Combines Graph Attention Networks with adversarial regularization to learn causal representations and an optimization-based generator to produce sparse, actionable counterfactual interventions for preventing bank defaults.
card.evaluation: Tested on large-scale synthetic ER and BA networks against baselines (LR, DebtRank, GCN, GAT); showed superior AUC, F1, and counterfactual plausibility.
card.limitation: Evaluated primarily on synthetic and semi-synthetic datasets due to financial data scarcity.
